svg.title: Mitosis and meiosis: chromosome behavior from one diploid parent
svg.desc: Source-specific teaching schematic, not a measurement. A parent with three red and three blue homologs duplicates chromosomes once on each branch. Mitosis aligns six individuals and separates sisters into two diploid daughters. Meiosis I pairs three bivalents and separates homologs into two cells with three duplicated chromosomes; meiosis II separates sisters into four haploid daughters. Final long/medium/short ancestry from left to right: red, red with blue tip, blue with red tip; red with blue tip, red, blue; blue, blue with red tip, red with blue tip; blue with red tip, blue, red. Cell contours and spindle fibers are simplified; chromosome sizes identify homologous classes.
